title: Bootstrapping Pion Form Factors at Large $N$
summary: We initiate a bootstrap study of pion form factors in large $N$ QCD. We consider the mixed system of the vector-current two-point function, the pion vector form factor, and the pion scattering amplitude in the chiral limit. At large $N$ these observables are meromorphic, with spectral data constrained by unitarity, crossing symmetry, and Regge boundedness. We obtain bounds of two kinds. The first are rigorous and universal: from analyticity, unitarity and the asymptotic Brodsky-Farrar scaling, we constrain low-energy form-factor coefficients. The second are more phenomenological, of the Shifman-Vainshtein-Zakharov type: feeding in the perturbative ultraviolet behavior at a finite scale lets us bound the pion decay constant, convert a large $N$ lattice measurement into a lower bound on the scale at which asymptotic freedom sets in, and constrain the pion charge radius. Combining these inputs, the space of allowed chiral Lagrangians shrinks toward the region where large $N$ QCD is expected to sit. Our results illustrate how local gauge-invariant probes provide a canonical bridge between the hadronic bootstrap and the microscopic QCD Lagrangian.

AI.tldr: This paper uses bootstrap methods at large N to study pion form factors, deriving rigorous and phenomenological bounds on low-energy observables from analyticity, unitarity, crossing symmetry, Regge behavior, and asymptotic scaling, bridging hadronic physics with the QCD Lagrangian.
AI.motivation: To constrain low-energy pion form factor coefficients and bridge the hadronic bootstrap approach with microscopic QCD using large N expansion and local gauge-invariant probes.
AI.method: Large N QCD bootstrap combining vector-current two-point function, pion vector form factor, and pion scattering amplitude; constraints from analyticity, unitarity, crossing symmetry, Regge boundedness, Brodsky-Farrar scaling, and perturbative UV input.
AI.result: Rigorous bounds from analyticity and asymptotic scaling; phenomenological SVZ-type bounds on the pion decay constant, asymptotic freedom scale, and pion charge radius; the allowed chiral Lagrangian space shrinks toward expected large N QCD region.
AI.conclusion: Local gauge-invariant probes provide a canonical bridge between the hadronic bootstrap and the microscopic QCD Lagrangian.

title: Calabi-Yau Orientifold Hypersurfaces and their F-theory Uplifts
summary: We present an algorithm that constructs Calabi-Yau threefold orientifolds and their $F$-theory uplifts to elliptically-fibered Calabi-Yau fourfolds, embedded in toric varieties at codimension one and two respectively. The resulting Calabi-Yau fourfolds arise from triangulations of $6d$ reflexive polytopes -- which our method constructs from orientifold data -- and are smooth away from isolated terminal singularities. For many of our fourfolds, the construction of the mirror manifold is immediate, enabling the computation of fourfold periods, and thus the seven-brane superpotential. We present multiple examples that demonstrate these capabilities. Our algorithms work with $\mathtt{CYTools}$ and are available through a GitHub repository.

The fourfolds are built from triangulations of 6d reflexive polytopes derived from orientifold data, are smooth except for isolated terminal singularities, and often allow immediate mirror construction for computing fourfold periods and seven-brane superpotentials. The algorithms integrate with CYTools and are publicly available on GitHub.
AI.motivation: To enable systematic construction of Calabi-Yau fourfolds from orientifold data for F-theory compactifications, and to facilitate computation of fourfold periods and seven-brane superpotentials via mirror symmetry.
AI.method: An algorithm that constructs Calabi-Yau threefold orientifolds and their F-theory uplifts to elliptically-fibered Calabi-Yau fourfolds embedded in toric varieties at codimension one and two. It uses triangulations of 6d reflexive polytopes constructed from orientifold data.
AI.result: The resulting Calabi-Yau fourfolds are smooth away from isolated terminal singularities; many allow immediate mirror construction, enabling fourfold period computation and seven-brane superpotential determination. Multiple examples demonstrate these capabilities.
AI.conclusion: The algorithms successfully bridge orientifold and F-theory constructions, providing a practical computational framework for studying Calabi-Yau fourfolds and their mirror manifolds, with implementations available via CYTools and GitHub.

title: Moduli Stabilisation for ADD and the Dark Dimension Scenario
summary: We provide a moduli stabilisation mechanism for realising anisotropic string compactifications with one or two large extra dimensions, corresponding to the ADD and Dark Dimension scenarios. This is achieved within the type IIB Large Volume Scenario, where an exponentially large Calabi-Yau volume in string units can naturally generate a parametrically low Kaluza-Klein scale. Anisotropy is realised by considering a Calabi-Yau threefold which is a K3 fibration over a $\mathbb{P}^1$ base. The volume of the 4D K3 fibre is stabilised at relatively small values by perturbative corrections to the effective action, in particular string loops and higher-derivative effects, leaving an exponentially large volume of the 2D $\mathbb{P}^1$ base. We argue that complex structure moduli stabilisation can dynamically deform the $\mathbb{P}^1$ base, corresponding to a Tyurin degeneration limit where the internal geometry effectively develops a single large 1D cycle. Within a unified description, the ADD case is instead recovered as a symmetric alternative limit. The potential can feature either a dS vacuum or a quintessence runaway, although in both cases some degree of tuning is required to match the observed cosmological constant scale. We also present an explicit Calabi-Yau orientifold example with consistent brane setup, tadpole cancellation and moduli stabilisation. We analyse the resulting moduli spectrum and associated phenomenological constraints, including supersymmetry breaking, cosmological moduli overproduction and fifth force bounds.

Using a K3-fibered Calabi-Yau threefold, perturbative corrections stabilize the K3 fiber small while the ℙ¹ base becomes exponentially large, with complex structure moduli enabling a Tyurin degeneration limit that yields a single large 1D cycle. The potential can produce dS vacua or quintessence, and the authors present an explicit orientifold example with consistent brane setup and phenomenological constraints.
AI.motivation: To provide a string theory realization of anisotropic extra-dimensional scenarios (ADD and Dark Dimension) by stabilizing moduli in a way that yields one or two large extra dimensions while keeping others small, addressing the hierarchy between the Planck scale and the fundamental scale.
AI.method: Type IIB Large Volume Scenario with a Calabi-Yau threefold that is a K3 fibration over a ℙ¹ base. Perturbative corrections (string loops and higher-derivative effects) stabilize the K3 fiber volume at small values while the ℙ¹ base volume is exponentially large. Complex structure moduli stabilization dynamically deforms the base via Tyurin degeneration to produce a single large 1D cycle.

The potential can feature either dS vacuum or quintessence runaway. Moduli spectrum and phenomenological constraints (supersymmetry breaking, cosmological moduli overproduction, fifth forces) are analyzed.
AI.conclusion: Anisotropic string compactifications with one or two large extra dimensions can be realized via moduli stabilization in K3-fibered Calabi-Yau manifolds, though tuning is required to match the observed cosmological constant scale.

title: Membrane instantons and non-perturbative effects in $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}/\mathrm{CFT}_{3}$
summary: We study Euclidean M2-brane instantons in Freund-Rubin backgrounds $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}\times \mathrm{Y}_7$. For a seven-dimensional weak $G_{2}$ manifold $\mathrm{Y}_7$, we show that the BPS condition for an M2-brane wrapping a three-cycle $Σ\subset \mathrm{Y}_7$ is equivalent to the associativity condition with respect to the nearly parallel $G_{2}$-structure. When $\mathrm{Y}_7$ is Sasaki-Einstein, we identify a special class of BPS M2-branes that preserve both real internal Killing spinors and correspond to invariant three-dimensional submanifolds inheriting a Sasakian structure. We analyse the quadratic fluctuations around BPS M2-brane instantons in these backgrounds. For the special class of M2-branes in Sasaki-Einstein manifolds, the fluctuation problem reduces to transversely elliptic complexes, and the one-loop partition function can be expressed in terms of the corresponding equivariant indices. We then apply the index formula for the one-loop partition function to invariant M2-branes in $S^{7}/\mathbb{Z}_{k}$, recovering the known result for the $S^3/\mathbb{Z}_k$ instantons and discussing more general invariant BPS cycles. As a further application, we consider M2-brane instantons with $S^3$-quotient worldvolumes in the $(p,q)$-model geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Euclidean M2-brane instantons in AdS4 × Y7 backgrounds, showing that BPS conditions correspond to associative cycles in weak G2 manifolds or invariant Sasakian submanifolds in Sasaki-Einstein spaces, and computes one-loop partition functions using equivariant indices.
AI.motivation: To understand the BPS conditions and quantum corrections of M2-brane instantons in Freund-Rubin compactifications, which are important for non-perturbative effects in M-theory and AdS/CFT correspondence.
AI.method: The authors analyze BPS conditions for M2-branes wrapping three-cycles in two classes of internal manifolds (weak G2 and Sasaki-Einstein), reduce fluctuation problems to transversely elliptic complexes, and apply index formulas to compute one-loop partition functions for specific geometries.
AI.result: BPS condition for M2-branes in weak G2 manifolds is equivalent to associativity; a special class in Sasaki-Einstein manifolds preserves real internal Killing spinors; one-loop partition functions are expressed via equivariant indices; recovered known S^3/Z_k result and applied to (p,q)-model geometry.
AI.conclusion: The formalism systematically computes M2-brane instanton effects in these backgrounds, matching known results and extending to more general cycles.

title: The next-to-leading order of the differential cross-section of the subprocess of Compton scattering of quark-gluon of prompt photon production in proton-proton collisions at NICA energies
summary:
In the presented article, the next-to-the-leading-order calculation of the differential cross-section of the Compton scattering subprocess $qg \rightarrow qγ$ for prompt photon production in proton-proton collisions at NICA energies has been carried out, both without and taking into account the longitudinal polarization of colliding protons.
  It is shown that the contribution of the next-to-leading order to the differential cross-section is significant at high energies of colliding protons and constitutes around $15\%$ of the leading-order calculation. The influence of the polarization of colliding protons on the next-to-leading-order calculation is more significant than on the leading-order calculation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a next-to-leading-order (NLO) calculation of the Compton scattering subprocess (qg → qγ) for prompt photon production in pp collisions at NICA energies, both with and without longitudinal proton polarization. The NLO contribution is ~15% of the LO cross-section at high energies, and polarization effects are more pronounced at NLO than LO.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical predictions for prompt photon production in proton-proton collisions at NICA energies by extending calculations beyond leading order, and to assess the impact of longitudinal proton polarization on these higher-order corrections.
AI.method: Next-to-leading-order perturbative QCD calculation of the differential cross-section for the Compton scattering subprocess qg → qγ, performed both with and without the inclusion of longitudinal polarization of colliding protons.
AI.result: The NLO contribution is significant (~15% of LO) at high collision energies. The effect of longitudinal proton polarization is more pronounced in the NLO calculation than in the LO calculation.
AI.conclusion: NLO corrections are non-negligible for accurate theoretical predictions of prompt photon production at NICA energies, and polarization effects must be accounted for at higher orders to achieve precision.

title: Generating Function of single-centered Black Hole Index in CHL Models
comment: 62 Pages, 7 Figures. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2510.05219
summary: We present the construction of the generating function of single-centered black hole index in general $\mathbb{Z}_N$ CHL models. This is done by subtracting from the index of quarter BPS dyons, described by a meromorphic Siegel modular form, the generating function for the index of two-centered black holes. We use black hole bound state metamorphosis in CHL models for the construction of the generating function of two-centered black hole index. We prove the convergence of the generating function for the cases $N=2,3$.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the generating function for single-centered black hole index in Z_N CHL models by subtracting two-centered contributions from the quarter BPS dyon index, using black hole bound state metamorphosis, and proves convergence for N=2,3.
AI.motivation: To accurately isolate and compute the index of single-centered black holes from the more complex quarter BPS dyon index, which includes contributions from two-centered bound states, in general Z_N CHL models.
AI.method: The authors subtract the two-centered black hole index (constructed via black hole bound state metamorphosis in CHL models) from the quarter BPS dyon index (described by a meromorphic Siegel modular form) to obtain the single-centered black hole generating function. Convergence is proved for N=2 and N=3.
AI.result: Successful construction of the generating function for single-centered black hole index in general Z_N CHL models, with proven convergence for N=2 and N=3.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a systematic method to isolate single-centered black hole indices in CHL models, verified for small N, enabling further study of black hole microstate counting.

title: Emergent Gauge Symmetries in Particle Physics and Cosmology
comment: Lectures presented at the 65. Jubilee Cracow School of Theoretical Physics, Zakopane, June 14-21 2025. 40 pages, to appear in Acta Physica Polonica B
summary: Where do gauge symmetries come from? These lectures develop the idea that the Standard Model might be emergent, with its gauge symmetries dissolving in some phase transition deep in the ultraviolet. The (meta-)stability of the Higgs vacuum may be pointing to some new critical phenomena at very high energy scales, with the Higgs connecting physics at LHC laboratory energies to that in the deep ultraviolet. In the emergence scenario, the dark energy scale comes out similar to the size of light Majorana neutrino masses. These two quantities appear at the same order in a low energy expansion in inverse powers of the scale of emergence, about $10^{16}$ GeV. Dark matter candidates include axions and phonon like excitations of degrees of freedom above the scale of emergence. Possible tests of these ideas involve neutrinos as well as gravitational-waves-related signals from the early Universe, which are sensitive to physics at very high energy scales.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that gauge symmetries of the Standard Model are not fundamental but emergent from a phase transition at high energy scales (~10^16 GeV), with the Higgs vacuum metastability pointing to critical phenomena in the UV. The dark energy scale naturally aligns with light Majorana neutrino masses in this framework, and dark matter candidates include axions and phonon-like excitations. Observational tests involve neutrinos and early-Universe gravitational waves.
AI.motivation: To address the origin of gauge symmetries in the Standard Model by exploring whether they dissolve in a UV phase transition, and to connect the Higgs vacuum metastability, dark energy scale, and neutrino masses within a unified emergent scenario.
AI.method: Theoretical framework developing the emergence scenario where the Standard Model gauge symmetries are not fundamental but emerge from a phase transition at high energy scales. The approach uses a low-energy expansion in inverse powers of the emergence scale (~10^16 GeV) and draws connections between Higgs vacuum metastability, dark energy, Majorana neutrino masses, and dark matter candidates.
AI.result: The dark energy scale appears at the same order as light Majorana neutrino masses in the low-energy expansion. The Higgs vacuum metastability may indicate critical phenomena at UV scales. Dark matter candidates include axions and phonon-like excitations from degrees of freedom above the emergence scale.
AI.conclusion: Gauge symmetries may be emergent rather than fundamental, with observational tests possible through neutrino physics and gravitational-wave signals from the early Universe that probe very high energy scales.

title: Operational Tube-Sector Theory of Quantum State Distinguishability Under Generalized Symmetries
summary: A variational principle for quantum-state distinguishability is established in many-body systems with generalized symmetries, including noninvertible cases described by fusion categories. Standard fidelity and symmetry-resolved diagnostics emerge as coarse-grained limits of a more refined operational structure. When symmetry actions terminate at entanglement cuts, distinguishability is governed by boundary tube algebras within a symmetry-constrained measurement resource theory. The physically admissible instruments are characterized by complete positivity, entanglement-cut locality, boundary-module covariance, and sequential stability. The resulting optimal measurement structure is uniquely fixed by the center of the boundary tube algebra, $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{phys}} = Z\!\left(\mathrm{Tube}_{\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{M}_A)\right)$, whose primitive idempotents define tube-sector probabilities that refine fidelity-based and symmetry-resolved descriptions. The associated tube positive-operator-valued measures (POVM) are extremal and yield optimal one-shot hypothesis-testing distinguishability under symmetry constraints. The construction is universal across fusion categories and independent of microscopic realization.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a variational principle for quantum-state distinguishability in many-body systems with generalized (including noninvertible) symmetries, showing that optimal measurement protocols are governed by the center of boundary tube algebras, yielding refined tube-sector probabilities and extremal POVMs that outperform standard fidelity and symmetry-resolved diagnostics.
AI.motivation: To develop a rigorous operational framework for quantum-state distinguishability in many-body systems with generalized symmetries (including noninvertible/fusion category symmetries), going beyond coarse-grained fidelity and symmetry-resolved measures to capture more refined structure.
AI.method: The authors formulate a symmetry-constrained measurement resource theory where admissible instruments satisfy complete positivity, entanglement-cut locality, boundary-module covariance, and sequential stability. They identify the optimal measurement structure as the center of the boundary tube algebra, $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{phys}} = Z(\mathrm{Tube}_{\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{M}_A))$, whose primitive idempotents define tube-sector probabilities.
AI.result: The resulting tube POVMs are extremal and yield optimal one-shot hypothesis-testing distinguishability under symmetry constraints. The construction is universal across fusion categories and independent of microscopic realization.
AI.conclusion: Standard fidelity and symmetry-resolved diagnostics are coarse-grained limits of this more refined operational structure. The center of the boundary tube algebra uniquely fixes the optimal measurement scheme.

title: LeWRON: Agentic Analysis of Electroweak Phase Transitions
summary: The electroweak phase transition (EWPT) is a central topic in particle physics and cosmology, connecting collider phenomenology, baryogenesis, and gravitational-wave observatories. Its analysis requires a technically demanding, convention-sensitive, and model-dependent pipeline, from constructing the finite-temperature effective potential to tracking thermal histories, computing bubble nucleation rates, and predicting gravitational-wave spectra. We present LeWRON (Learning ElectroWeak phase tRansitiON), an agentic framework that orchestrates this pipeline starting from an input Lagrangian. LeWRON combines audited toolbox construction with an Explorer module that uses the generated model-specific code for further analysis, including scans and plots. Intermediate analytic outputs are checked by auditor agents and stored as structured artifacts, enabling reproducible human inspection and downstream use through both a command-line interface and a public Python API. The framework supports a reproduction mode, which infers conventions from the literature and reproduces published results, and a discovery mode, which guides users through structured checkpoints for new models. We demonstrate LeWRON across representative beyond-the-Standard-Model scenarios and release the code on GitHub.

AI.tldr: LeWRON is an automated agentic framework that orchestrates the full electroweak phase transition analysis pipeline from input Lagrangian to gravitational-wave spectra, with auditing, reproduction, and discovery modes.
AI.motivation: The EWPT analysis pipeline is technically demanding, convention-sensitive, and model-dependent, requiring integration of multiple complex steps (finite-temperature effective potential, thermal history, bubble nucleation, gravitational-wave spectra) that are prone to errors and lack reproducibility.
AI.method: LeWRON combines an audited toolbox construction module with an Explorer module for scans/plots; uses auditor agents to check intermediate analytic outputs stored as structured artifacts; supports reproduction mode (infers conventions from literature) and discovery mode (structured checkpoints for new models); provides CLI and Python API.
AI.result: Demonstrated across representative beyond-the-Standard-Model scenarios; code released on GitHub; enables reproducible human inspection and downstream use.
AI.conclusion: LeWRON provides a complete, audited, and reproducible agentic framework that automates the EWPT analysis pipeline, bridging the gap between Lagrangian input and observable predictions while ensuring convention consistency and human verifiability.

title: Quantum models with the Yang-Lee phase transition
summary: In this article, we present four different $1+1$D quantum models that realize the Yang-Lee (YL) phase transition under a deformation that preserves $PT$ symmetry. These are the antiferromagnetic Ising spin chain in transverse and longitudinal magnetic fields, the massive Schwinger model, the Blume-Capel model, and the three-state quantum clock model. Using the state-operator correspondence, we identify the YL critical point, compute the scaling dimensions of the lowest operators in each model, and find perfect agreement with the exact results for the YL criticality in two dimensions. Using bosonization for the Schwinger model and the Polyakov-Hubbard transformation for the other models, we show that in all of these quantum models the YL critical point is described, as expected, by a massless bosonic field with an $i φ^3$ interaction. In the quantum clock model, this critical field interacts with a massive bosonic field, and we identify the massless and massive states in the Hamiltonian spectrum. In addition, we numerically compute the two-point function of $φ$ at the Yang-Lee critical point and show that it grows with distance, in agreement with theoretical expectations.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates four 1+1D quantum models (antiferromagnetic Ising chain, massive Schwinger model, Blume-Capel model, and three-state quantum clock model) that exhibit Yang-Lee criticality under PT-symmetric deformation, confirming the universality class via scaling dimensions, bosonization, and numerical two-point functions.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that the Yang-Lee (YL) phase transition, a non-unitary critical phenomenon, can be realized in multiple 1+1D quantum models under PT-symmetric deformations, and to verify the universal description of YL criticality via a massless bosonic field with an iφ³ interaction.
AI.method: The authors use the state-operator correspondence to identify YL critical points and compute scaling dimensions. They employ bosonization for the Schwinger model and the Polyakov-Hubbard transformation for the other models. Numerical computation of the two-point function of φ at the YL critical point is also performed.
AI.result: All four models exhibit perfect agreement with exact results for YL criticality in 2D. The YL critical point is described by a massless bosonic field with an iφ³ interaction. In the quantum clock model, a coupled massive bosonic field is identified. The two-point function of φ grows with distance, confirming theoretical expectations.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes multiple lattice and continuum realizations of Yang-Lee criticality in 1+1D quantum systems under PT-symmetric deformations, confirming the universality class and its description by the iφ³ theory.

title: Partial-wave unitarity and long-range interactions
summary: Theories with massless particles contain $t$-channel (forward scattering) singularities that cause standard fixed order expressions for partial-wave amplitudes to be ill-defined. This presents an obstruction to systematically improvable partial-wave unitarity bounds. In this work, we study the construction of partial-wave amplitudes in a modified perturbation theory that incorporates long-range interactions focusing on the role of off-shell Coulomb modes. We find that there exists a universal description of the forward scattering region that renders the amplitudes renormalization scale independent. The resulting partial-wave amplitudes become well defined single-scale objects without spurious dependence on the infrared regulator, and we present a practical method for their computation order-by-order in perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses t-channel singularities in partial-wave amplitudes for massless particle theories by developing a modified perturbation theory that incorporates off-shell Coulomb modes, yielding well-defined, renormalization-scale-independent partial-wave amplitudes suitable for systematic unitarity bounds.
AI.motivation: Fixed-order partial-wave amplitudes for massless particles suffer from t-channel (forward scattering) singularities, making standard perturbative expressions ill-defined and obstructing systematic partial-wave unitarity bounds.
AI.method: The authors construct partial-wave amplitudes in a modified perturbation theory that includes long-range interactions, specifically focusing on off-shell Coulomb modes, and develop a practical order-by-order computational method.
AI.result: A universal description of the forward scattering region is found that eliminates renormalization scale dependence, producing well-defined, single-scale partial-wave amplitudes free from spurious infrared regulator dependence.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method provides a systematic framework for computing partial-wave amplitudes order-by-order in perturbation theory, enabling rigorous unitarity bounds in theories with massless particles.

title: Factorized Quantum Curves and Voronoi Polytopes in 3D Duality Cascades with FI Parameters
summary: In the study of duality cascades in three-dimensional gauge theories without FI parameters, an important role is played by a fundamental domain whose vertices correspond to brane configurations with vanishing relative ranks. Through the Fermi gas formalism, such brane configurations are known to be represented by factorized quantum curves. In this paper, we show that this factorized description extends naturally to quantum curves associated with del Pezzo geometries possessing exceptional Weyl-group symmetries in the presence of FI parameters. We find that the vertices of the corresponding fundamental domains, identified with Voronoi polytopes of exceptional root lattices, are realized as factorized quantum curves built from canonical operators interpreted as 5-branes dressed with FI parameters. This provides a physical realization of the vertices of the Voronoi polytopes as ``extremal'' brane configurations.

AI.tldr: The paper extends the factorized quantum curve description of duality cascades in 3D gauge theories to del Pezzo geometries with exceptional Weyl-group symmetries, showing that Voronoi polytope vertices correspond to extremal brane configurations dressed with FI parameters.
AI.motivation: To extend the factorized quantum curve description of duality cascades—originally developed for theories without FI parameters—to del Pezzo geometries with exceptional Weyl-group symmetries in the presence of FI parameters.
AI.method: Using the Fermi gas formalism and factorized quantum curves, the authors identify fundamental domain vertices with Voronoi polytopes of exceptional root lattices, realized as factorized quantum curves built from canonical operators interpreted as 5-branes dressed with FI parameters.
AI.result: The factorized description extends naturally to del Pezzo geometries with exceptional Weyl-group symmetries when FI parameters are present. The vertices of Voronoi polytopes are realized as factorized quantum curves corresponding to extremal brane configurations.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a physical realization of Voronoi polytope vertices as extremal brane configurations dressed with FI parameters, unifying the description of duality cascades across a broader class of geometries.

title: From Rags to Jeans: Axion Miniclusters from Early matter domination
summary: In an early matter-dominated era, density and temperature inhomogeneities of the radiation bath grow more efficiently than in the standard radiation-dominated history. If the axion mass depends on temperature, these inhomogeneities induce spatial fluctuations of the axion mass, providing a new source term for axion density perturbations. We show that this mechanism is most efficient when the reheating temperature lies just below the mass-saturation scale $T_Λ$, and can drive axion overdensities to order unity by matter--radiation equality. For the QCD axion saturating the observed dark matter abundance, the nonlinear spectrum at equality exhibits two characteristic regions: one associated with the gravitational enhancement already present in moduli-driven cosmologies, and another produced by the temperature dependence of the axion mass. We estimate the resulting minicluster masses and discuss the possible formation of axion miniclusters and axion-star substructure.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that in an early matter-dominated era, temperature-dependent axion mass fluctuations driven by radiation inhomogeneities can produce order-unity axion overdensities by matter-radiation equality, leading to distinctive minicluster and axion star formation patterns for QCD axion dark matter.
AI.motivation: To investigate a new mechanism for generating axion density perturbations arising from the temperature dependence of the axion mass in early matter-dominated cosmologies, beyond standard gravitational effects.
AI.method: Analytical calculations of perturbation growth in an early matter-dominated era with temperature-dependent axion mass, examining the spatial fluctuations of the axion mass induced by radiation bath inhomogeneities and their impact on axion density perturbations.
AI.result: The mechanism is most efficient when the reheating temperature is just below the mass-saturation scale T_Λ, and can drive axion overdensities to order unity by matter-radiation equality. The nonlinear spectrum at equality shows two characteristic regions: one from gravitational enhancement and another from the temperature-dependent axion mass.
AI.conclusion: Temperature-dependent axion mass fluctuations in early matter-dominated eras provide a new, efficient source of axion density perturbations, with implications for minicluster masses and the possible formation of axion miniclusters and axion-star substructure.

title: Metastable and critical-bubble branches of Coleman--Weinberg monopoles
summary: We revisit the Coleman--Weinberg monopole problem introduced by Kiselev, where radiative symmetry breaking makes the broken vacuum metastable. We construct the associated static monopole--critical-bubble configuration in the full coupled radial Higgs--gauge system and show that it is a saddle of the static energy functional. The metastable monopole and monopole--critical-bubble branches are characterized by their profiles, energies, and radial Hessian spectra. The monopole--bubble solution carries a negative radial mode, while the metastable monopole remains locally stable until its lowest radial Hessian eigenvalue approaches zero. The resulting branch structure gives a direct static picture of how Coleman--Weinberg monopoles lose metastability, with critical rescaled scalar mass parameter \(μ_c=0.064352(1)\).

AI.tldr: This paper revisits the Coleman-Weinberg monopole problem, constructing the static monopole-critical-bubble configuration in a coupled Higgs-gauge system. It shows the bubble is a saddle of the static energy functional, characterizes both branches via profiles/energies/radial Hessian spectra, and finds that the monopole-bubble carries a negative radial mode while the metastable monopole remains stable until its lowest eigenvalue vanishes. The critical rescaled scalar mass parameter is determined as μ_c=0.064352(1).
AI.motivation: To understand the metastability loss of Coleman-Weinberg monopoles through radiative symmetry breaking, extending Kiselev's work by constructing the full static monopole-critical-bubble configuration in the coupled radial Higgs-gauge system.
AI.method: The authors construct the static monopole-critical-bubble configuration in the full coupled radial Higgs-gauge system, analyze it as a saddle of the static energy functional, and characterize both the metastable monopole and monopole-critical-bubble branches using profiles, energies, and radial Hessian spectra.
AI.result: The monopole-bubble solution has a negative radial mode; the metastable monopole is locally stable until its lowest radial Hessian eigenvalue reaches zero; the critical rescaled scalar mass parameter is μ_c=0.064352(1).
AI.conclusion: The branch structure provides a direct static picture of how Coleman-Weinberg monopoles lose metastability, with a precisely determined critical mass parameter.

title: Spin Identification of Dark Sector Mediators through Angular Distributions
summary: A variety of experiments are operating or planned to search for displaced decays of light long-lived dark sector particles. In case such a state is discovered, the next step is determining its quantum numbers. We identify an angular observable, reconstructible solely from the decay products' four-momenta, that exhibits an anisotropic distribution for vector bosons from light meson decays and an isotropic distribution for scalars. We demonstrate that searches at DUNE, SHiP and FASER2 will be able to identify the mediator spin in sizable regions of yet unconstrained parameter space.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an angular observable that can distinguish between vector and scalar mediators produced in light meson decays, based solely on the four-momenta of decay products, and shows that future experiments (DUNE, SHiP, FASER2) can determine mediator spin in large unconstrained parameter regions.
AI.motivation: Once a long-lived dark sector particle is discovered, determining its quantum numbers (particularly spin) becomes the next crucial step, but no method existed for distinguishing scalar vs. vector mediators using only displaced decay products' kinematics.
AI.method: The authors identify an angular observable constructed purely from the four-momenta of the decay products, which exhibits anisotropic distributions for vector bosons from light meson decays and isotropic distributions for scalars. They simulate sensitivity at DUNE, SHiP, and FASER2.
AI.result: The angular observable clearly differentiates vector (anisotropic) from scalar (isotropic) mediators. Future experiments DUNE, SHiP, and FASER2 can measure this observable and determine mediator spin in significant regions of currently unconstrained parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The proposed spin-discriminating observable enables future long-lived particle searches to go beyond discovery and characterize the quantum numbers of dark sector mediators, providing a path to identify the nature of new physics.

title: Leading UV Formula for Finite-Volume Vertex Operator Expectation Values in the Sine-Gordon Model from Kink NLIE
summary:
We study the ultraviolet (UV) limit of finite-volume expectation values of vertex operators in the sine-Gordon model using the kink nonlinear integral equation (NLIE) description of the conformal limit.
  By analysing the integrable formulation of vacuum expectation values in the small-volume regime, we conjecture an explicit analytic expression for the leading asymptotic term in the small-volume expansion, formulated in terms of kink functions. This establishes a direct connection between the integrable finite-volume description and the expected conformal asymptotics determined by the 3-point functions of the underlying conformal field theory (CFT).
  The proposed formula is tested against the analytic expression known from complex Liouville conformal field theory using high-precision numerics, showing agreement to at least 19 significant digits.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the UV limit of vertex operator expectation values in the sine-Gordon model using the kink NLIE, conjectures an explicit leading asymptotic term for small-volume expansion in terms of kink functions, and verifies it against complex Liouville CFT predictions with 19-digit precision.
AI.motivation: To establish a direct connection between the integrable finite-volume description (via kink NLIE) and the conformal asymptotics determined by 3-point functions of the underlying CFT.
AI.method: Analysis of the integrable formulation of vacuum expectation values via the kink nonlinear integral equation (NLIE) in the small-volume (UV) regime; conjecture of an explicit analytic asymptotic expression tested against complex Liouville CFT via high-precision numerics.
AI.result: The conjectured asymptotic formula agrees with analytic predictions from complex Liouville CFT to at least 19 significant digits.
AI.conclusion: The proposed kink-function-based asymptotic expression correctly captures the conformal limit, bridging the integrable NLIE description and the underlying CFT 3-point functions with extremely high numerical precision.

title: Real and Virtual Propagation in Neutrino Oscillations
summary: We revisit flavor oscillations in vacuum in terms of the propagation time of intermediate states. In the limit of a long propagation time (or distance), degenerate intermediate states exhibit oscillatory behavior, as described by the Jacob--Sachs (or Grimus--Stockinger) theorem within wave-packet quantum field theory. By explicitly evaluating the relevant integrals using the saddle-point method, we derive an extended expression for the flavor-changing amplitude that remains valid even for shorter propagation times. We show that oscillations occur only when the propagation time exceeds a threshold set by the energy uncertainty of the external wave packets and by the decay width of the propagating particle. For shorter propagation, the intermediate particle behaves as a purely virtual state, in the sense that it cannot propagate over a macroscopic distance. Although a direct experimental test of the transition from virtual to real propagation is challenging, since it typically occurs at microscopic scales, our result implies that the Jacob--Sachs theorem holds to higher accuracy than previously expected, even at short propagation times. Our formalism applies not only to neutrinos but also to other propagating particles, and future improvements in energy resolution may make this threshold observable.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits flavor oscillations in vacuum by analyzing propagation time of intermediate states. Using saddle-point methods, the authors derive an extended flavor-changing amplitude valid for shorter propagation times, showing oscillations only occur beyond a threshold set by energy uncertainty and decay width. Below threshold, the intermediate particle behaves as a purely virtual state.
AI.motivation: To understand the transition from virtual to real propagation in flavor oscillations and derive a formalism that remains valid for short propagation times, where the standard Jacob-Sachs/Grimus-Stockinger theorem assumptions break down.
AI.method: The authors use saddle-point method to explicitly evaluate integrals relevant to flavor-changing amplitudes, extending the standard wave-packet quantum field theory approach beyond the long-propagation-time limit.
AI.result: Flavor oscillations only occur when propagation time exceeds a threshold determined by the energy uncertainty of external wave packets and the decay width of the propagating particle. Below this threshold, the intermediate particle behaves as a purely virtual state incapable of macroscopic propagation.
AI.conclusion: The Jacob-Sachs theorem holds to higher accuracy than previously expected even at short times. The formalism applies broadly to any propagating particles (not just neutrinos), and future improvements in energy resolution could make the threshold observable.

title: Quantization of Brane-Skyrmions via Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: In this work, we investigate the canonical quantization of topological solitons appearing in braneworld scenarios. In particular, we focus on Brane-Skyrmions, topological field configurations analogous to standard Skyrmions, which emerge as solutions of the Dirac-Nambu-Goto action supplemented by an induced curvature term. By quantizing the (iso)spin collective coordinates of the Brane-Skyrmion, we obtain a Hamiltonian that we solve perturbatively via an expansion in powers of $J^2$, in contrast to the standard Skyrme model. Furthermore, we implement a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to determine the soliton profile that minimizes the energy, consistently incorporating the backreaction from the quantized spin degrees of freedom. We conclude with a discussion of the potential applications of this framework to the description of hadronic spectra. Our results highlight both the theoretical potential of brane-defect models and the growing role of neural network methods in theoretical physics.

AI.tldr: This paper canonically quantizes Brane-Skyrmions (topological solitons in braneworlds) using collective coordinate quantization with perturbative expansion in J², and employs a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to find the energy-minimizing soliton profile with backreaction from quantized spin.
AI.motivation: To extend canonical quantization techniques from standard Skyrmions to topological solitons in braneworld scenarios, specifically Brane-Skyrmions derived from the Dirac-Nambu-Goto action with induced curvature.
AI.method: Quantization of (iso)spin collective coordinates of Brane-Skyrmions, perturbative Hamiltonian expansion in powers of J² (contrasting with the standard Skyrme model), and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to determine the soliton profile that minimizes energy while incorporating backreaction from quantized spin.
AI.result: A perturbatively solvable Hamiltonian for quantized Brane-Skyrmions, with PINN-derived soliton profiles that consistently account for backreaction effects from quantized spin degrees of freedom.
AI.conclusion: The framework shows theoretical potential for brane-defect models and applications to hadronic spectra, while demonstrating the growing utility of neural network methods in theoretical physics.

title: Freeze-in at all couplings
summary: We perform a comprehensive analysis of a charged parent freeze-in dark matter model, focusing on scenarios where the Universe reheats to a temperature comparable to or lower than the mass scales of the theory. In such configurations, dark matter production is Boltzmann-suppressed, allowing for stronger couplings between dark matter and the Standard Model thermal bath while still reproducing the observed relic abundance. We emphasize the non-trivial interplay between the reheating temperature, the mediator and dark matter masses and the coupling strength. We show that tracking the number density evolution of both dark matter and the mediator is essential to obtain reliable predictions, including unexpected behaviors such as the mediator non-equilibration due to fast decays. Lastly, we explore the phenomenological implications of this scenario, updating constraints from LHC searches and lepton flavour-violating decays and highlighting the complementarity of these searches in probing the cosmologically viable parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a charged parent freeze-in dark matter model with low reheating temperatures, finding that Boltzmann suppression allows stronger DM-SM couplings while maintaining relic abundance, and shows the importance of tracking both DM and mediator number densities, with updated LHC and lepton flavor-violating constraints.
AI.motivation: To study freeze-in dark matter production in scenarios where the reheating temperature is comparable to or lower than the mass scales, where Boltzmann suppression permits stronger couplings while still achieving the observed relic abundance.
AI.method: Comprehensive analysis of a charged parent freeze-in DM model with low reheating temperatures; tracking number density evolution of both DM and mediator; updating phenomenological constraints from LHC searches and lepton flavour-violating decays.
AI.result: Stronger couplings between DM and the SM thermal bath are viable due to Boltzmann suppression at low reheating temperatures; the mediator may fail to equilibrate due to fast decays, leading to unexpected behaviors; updated constraints from LHC and lepton flavour-violating searches show complementarity in probing viable parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The interplay between reheating temperature, mediator/DM masses, and coupling strength is non-trivial; simultaneously tracking DM and mediator evolution is essential for reliable predictions; collider and flavor constraints are complementary in probing the cosmologically allowed parameter space.

title: Higher-loop wormhole length in sine-dilaton gravity from DSSYK Krylov complexity
summary: The quantum wormhole length in sine-dilaton gravity has been shown to equal the Krylov spread complexity in the double-scaled SYK model. In the infinite temperature limit, we compute the five-loop semiclassical expansion of DSSYK complexity by singular perturbation of the operator Liouville-type equations of motion, extending the existing one-loop results. The same method is applied to evaluate the Krylov variance and third-order cumulant, related to the connected two- and three-point functions of the length operator at coincident points. The small- and large-time behaviour of these observables is also studied. In particular, for the large-time slope of the wormhole linear growth, we provide a conjecture for the resummation of the perturbative series, and discuss non-perturbative corrections revealed by numerical data.

AI.tldr: The paper extends the semiclassical expansion of Krylov spread complexity in double-scaled SYK model to five loops, computes Krylov variance and third-order cumulant via singular perturbation of Liouville-type equations, and proposes a resummation conjecture for the wormhole's linear growth slope with non-perturbative corrections.
AI.motivation: To derive higher-loop semiclassical corrections to Krylov spread complexity and related observables in DSSYK, beyond the existing one-loop results, and to understand the resummation and non-perturbative structure of the wormhole length growth.
AI.method: Singular perturbation theory applied to operator Liouville-type equations of motion, computing five-loop semiclassical expansion; numerical analysis for non-perturbative corrections.
AI.result: Five-loop semiclassical expansion for Krylov complexity; Krylov variance and third-order cumulant from connected two- and three-point functions of the length operator; small- and large-time behavior; a conjectured resummation for the large-time slope and identification of non-perturbative corrections.
AI.conclusion: The perturbative series for wormhole linear growth slope may be resummable, with non-perturbative effects visible in numerical data, deepening the quantum gravity–complexity correspondence.

title: Sensitivity of the photon-induced processes to the proton radius
summary: We study the exclusive production of dileptons in proton--proton collisions as a probe of the proton radius. Using a dipole form factor model, we compare the conventional choice of $Λ^2=0.71$~GeV$^2$ with PDG test scenarios corresponding to $r_p=0.8751$~fm and $r_p=0.84087$~fm. The sensitivity is greatest at large dilepton invariant masses and forward/backward rapidity. Fitting to the current ATLAS and CMS data within the adopted model gives $Λ^2 = 0.465 \pm 0.056~\mathrm{GeV}^2$, corresponding to an effective radius $r_p = 1.002 \pm 0.038~\mathrm{fm}$, which indicates non-trivial sensitivity on the proton radius scale, but is not yet a definitive solution to the proton radius puzzle.

AI.tldr: This paper studies dilepton production in proton-proton collisions as a probe of the proton radius, finding sensitivity at large invariant masses and forward/backward rapidity, but the fitted effective radius (1.002 ± 0.038 fm) from current ATLAS/CMS data does not resolve the proton radius puzzle.
AI.motivation: To use exclusive dilepton production in proton-proton collisions as a probe of the proton radius, aiming to address the proton radius puzzle.
AI.method: Using a dipole form factor model, comparing conventional Λ²=0.71 GeV² with PDG test scenarios (rp=0.8751 fm and rp=0.84087 fm), and fitting to ATLAS and CMS data.
AI.result: Fitting yields Λ² = 0.465 ± 0.056 GeV², corresponding to effective radius rp = 1.002 ± 0.038 fm, showing non-trivial sensitivity but not a definitive solution.
AI.conclusion: The approach shows sensitivity to the proton radius scale, especially at large dilepton invariant masses and forward/backward rapidity, but current data does not resolve the proton radius puzzle.

title: Macroscopic Black-Hole Remnants in a Nonlocal Field Theory: Towards Hawking Radiation in SFT
summary: We demonstrate that, for a large black hole of radius $a$, Hawking radiation terminates around the scrambling time $u_{\text{scr}} \equiv 2a \log(a/\ell)$ due to the nonlocal, exponential suppression of trans-Planckian interactions inherent in string field theory (SFT). Modifying a massless scalar field's interaction with a dynamical black hole background via the smearing operator $e^{\ell^2\Box}$ (where $\ell$ denotes the string length scale), we calculate the time-dependent number expectation value $\langle \hat{N}(u) \rangle$ of outgoing Hawking particles at retarded time $u$. While the standard Planck spectrum at the Hawking temperature is reproduced at early times ($u \ll u_{\text{scr}}$), the particle number approaches zero shortly after the scrambling time. This early shutoff reflects the property that the collapsing shell becomes effectively invisible to trans-Planckian modes, offering an alternative resolution to the black hole information paradox via a macroscopic remnant.

AI.tldr: For a large black hole of radius a, Hawking radiation terminates around the scrambling time u_scr = 2a log(a/ℓ) due to nonlocal, exponential suppression of trans-Planckian interactions in string field theory, offering an alternative resolution to the information paradox via a macroscopic remnant.
AI.motivation: To address the black hole information paradox by demonstrating that Hawking radiation shuts off early, preventing the complete evaporation that leads to information loss.
AI.method: Modifying a massless scalar field's interaction with a dynamical black hole background using the smearing operator e^{ℓ²□} from string field theory, then calculating the time-dependent number expectation value ⟨N̂(u)⟩ of outgoing Hawking particles.
AI.result: The standard Planck spectrum at Hawking temperature is reproduced at early times (u ≪ u_scr), but the particle number approaches zero shortly after the scrambling time u_scr = 2a log(a/ℓ).
AI.conclusion: The collapsing shell becomes effectively invisible to trans-Planckian modes, allowing black hole evaporation to stop early and leave a macroscopic remnant, offering an alternative resolution to the information paradox.

title: $U(1)_{B-L}$ Dark Matter Constrains Smooth (SUSY) Hybrid Inflation
summary: We propose a unified framework that connects inflationary dynamics with dark matter production within a supersymmetric $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model. The setup is based on smooth hybrid inflation embedded in supergravity, with a non-minimal Kahler potential ensuring control of higher-order corrections. The model involves three scalar fields: the inflaton $σ$, an auxiliary field $ζ$ responsible for ending inflation, and a singlet mediator $η$ that links the inflationary and dark sectors. Dark matter is realized as an inert scalar stabilized by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry and produced non-thermally via reheating dynamics. We show that reproducing the observed dark matter relic abundance imposes strong constraints on the inflationary sector, significantly reducing the allowed parameter space. As a result, the scalar spectral index is tightly constrained to $n_s \simeq 0.972 - 0.974$, consistent with current observational bounds. While the inflaton-dark matter coupling has a negligible effect on the background evolution, it induces observable modifications in the tensor-to-scalar ratio and the spectrum of primordial gravitational waves. This establishes a direct link between dark matter physics and inflationary observables.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified framework connecting inflationary dynamics with dark matter production in a supersymmetric $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model. The model links inflationary observables (especially $n_s \simeq 0.972-0.974$) to dark matter relic abundance through non-thermal production mediated by a singlet field, with observable imprints on tensor-to-scalar ratio and primordial gravitational waves.
AI.motivation: To establish a direct theoretical and observational link between inflationary dynamics and dark matter production within a consistent supersymmetric framework, addressing both the early universe expansion and the dark matter relic abundance problem.
AI.method: The authors embed smooth hybrid inflation in supergravity with a non-minimal Kähler potential to control higher-order corrections. The model includes three scalar fields: inflaton $\sigma$, auxiliary field $\zeta$ (ending inflation), and singlet mediator $\eta$ linking inflation and dark sectors. Dark matter is an inert scalar stabilized by $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, produced non-thermally via reheating dynamics.
AI.result: The observed dark matter relic abundance severely constrains the inflationary parameter space, yielding a scalar spectral index tightly bounded to $n_s \simeq 0.972-0.974$. The inflaton-dark matter coupling negligibly affects background evolution but modifies the tensor-to-scalar ratio and primordial gravitational wave spectrum observably.
AI.conclusion: A direct link exists between dark matter physics and inflationary observables. The dark matter relic abundance constraint significantly reduces the allowed inflationary parameter space, enabling cross-probes of inflation and dark matter through cosmic microwave background and gravitational wave observations.

title: The magic of the gravitational vacuum
comment: 23 pages, 6 figures, Contribution to `Narlikar's Steady World: Man and the Legend'
summary: The black hole information paradox challenges us to do something that is seemingly impossible: find a violation of the semiclassical approximation in a region where all curvatures are low. The vecro hypothesis proposes a structure of the gravitational vacuum that can accomplish this task. In this article we explain the hypothesis, and give a lattice model to describe the essence of its idea. The Hamiltonian of the model is completely local, but the vacuum exhibits correlations among planck scale fluctuations which fall off relatively slowly with distance. These extended-scale correlations are able to `feel around' the region where a closed trapped surface is about to form, and to react by nucleating fuzzball structure that destroys semiclassical spacetime.

AI.tldr: The paper explains the vecro hypothesis, which proposes that gravitational vacuum correlations at the Planck scale extend over large distances and can trigger fuzzball formation to resolve the black hole information paradox, demonstrated through a local lattice model.
AI.motivation: To address the black hole information paradox by finding a mechanism that violates semiclassical gravity in low-curvature regions, which seems impossible under standard assumptions.
AI.method: Proposes the vecro hypothesis of gravitational vacuum structure and constructs a local lattice model whose vacuum exhibits Planck-scale correlations that decay slowly with distance, enabling nonlocal effects through local interactions.
AI.result: The lattice model shows that extended-scale correlations in the vacuum can detect the impending formation of a closed trapped surface and respond by nucleating fuzzball structure, destroying semiclassical spacetime.
AI.conclusion: The vecro hypothesis provides a plausible resolution to the black hole information paradox by showing how Planck-scale vacuum correlations can lead to semiclassical violation in low-curvature regions, with the lattice model demonstrating the feasibility of this mechanism.

title: Charged Lepton Flavor Violation at Neutrino Telescopes
summary: Any observation of charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV) would be a clear signal of beyond-the-Standard-Model physics. Here, we propose a novel CLFV search using neutrino telescopes with their large cosmic-ray muon samples. Specifically, we use a recent IceCube cosmic-ray muon dataset and propose a new search for muon-to-tau conversion inside the IceCube detector. We illustrate our idea with CLFV interactions described by model-independent Effective Field Theory (EFT) operators and present the IceCube sensitivity on the relevant EFT scale. We also consider a specific realization of the EFT operator in terms of an axial-vector $Z'$ interaction and show sensitivities in the $Z'$ mass-coupling plane. We compare our sensitivities with those from low-energy CLFV searches, as well as from current and future collider experiments. We also show projections from next-generation neutrino telescopes, such as IceCube-Gen2 and HUNT, and demonstrate how neutrino telescopes can provide a powerful complementary probe of CLFV.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using neutrino telescopes (IceCube and future detectors) to search for charged lepton flavor violation via muon-to-tau conversion in cosmic-ray muon datasets, using EFT and Z' model frameworks, and shows competitive sensitivities complementary to low-energy and collider searches.
AI.motivation: Charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV) is a clear sign of physics beyond the Standard Model, yet has not been observed. The authors aim to explore a novel method to search for CLFV using existing and future neutrino telescope data, specifically muon-to-tau conversion in IceCube's large cosmic-ray muon sample.
AI.method: The authors propose using a recent IceCube cosmic-ray muon dataset to search for muon-to-tau conversion. They model the CLFV interactions using model-independent Effective Field Theory (EFT) operators and also consider a specific realization via an axial-vector Z' interaction. Sensitivities are computed for the EFT scale and the Z' mass-coupling parameter space.
AI.result: The paper presents IceCube's sensitivity to the EFT scale for CLFV operators and shows sensitivities in the Z' mass-coupling plane. Comparisons are made with low-energy CLFV searches and current/future collider experiments. Projections for next-generation neutrino telescopes (IceCube-Gen2, HUNT) demonstrate improved reach.
AI.conclusion: Neutrino telescopes can serve as powerful complementary probes of CLFV, offering sensitivities that compete with and extend beyond traditional low-energy and collider-based searches, especially with next-generation detectors.

title: Fortuity beyond counting: an explicit construction
summary: We reconsider the "fortuity'' mechanism in the D1D5 CFT focusing on the K3 symmetric orbifold. Going beyond the counting of BPS states, we investigate perturbatively how the explicit form of the BPS cohomologies is modified by the twist-two deformations. We calculate the action of the supercharges in the sector $(h,j)=(1,0)$ for different values of the central charge and derive explicit expressions for the primary states. Equipped with this information, we compare some protected three-point couplings in the free and the gravity regime. We show that agreement between the two descriptions imposes non-trivial constraints on the identification of monotone and fortuitous states. In particular, we argue that the map relating theories with different values of the central charge must and can be defined so as to commute with the supercharges that define the cochain complex. We then study the three-point correlators between the fortuitous and monotone states identified in our analysis to assess whether the two sectors are dynamically decoupled. We find an explicit example of a non-vanishing coupling between two monotone and a fortuitous state, providing evidence that the two sectors are dynamically connected.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits the fortuity mechanism in D1D5 CFT (K3 symmetric orbifold), analyzing how twist-two deformations modify BPS cohomologies. It computes supercharge actions in the (h,j)=(1,0) sector, compares protected three-point couplings between free and gravity regimes, and finds evidence that monotone and fortuitous states are dynamically connected through a non-vanishing coupling.
AI.motivation: To understand the fortuity mechanism in D1D5 CFT beyond BPS state counting, specifically how the explicit form of BPS cohomologies changes under twist-two deformations, and to assess whether monotone and fortuitous sectors are dynamically decoupled.
AI.method: Perturbative analysis of BPS cohomologies under twist-two deformations; calculation of supercharge action in the (h,j)=(1,0) sector for varying central charge; comparison of protected three-point couplings in free vs. gravity regimes; identification of constraints on the mapping between theories with different central charges.
AI.result: Agreement between free and gravity descriptions imposes non-trivial constraints on identification of monotone and fortuitous states. The map relating theories with different central charges must be defined to commute with supercharges. An explicit non-vanishing three-point coupling between two monotone and one fortuitous state was found.
AI.conclusion: The monotone and fortuitous sectors are dynamically connected, as evidenced by a non-vanishing coupling between them, contrary to the possibility of dynamical decoupling.

title: Constraining ADD black holes at the LHC with $\sqrt{s} = 14$ TeV
summary: We explore microscopic black holes at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in the context of the ADD model for the centre-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s} = 14~\mathrm{TeV}$ at an integrated luminosity of $349.4~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ and provide constraints on the black hole mass, $M_{\mathrm{B}}$ by taking into account the effects of loss during the formation process of black holes through the parameter $ζ$. Our analysis reveals that for $ζ= 0$, black holes with $M_{\mathrm{B}} \leq 11.83~\mathrm{TeV}$ are disfavored in the case of three extra dimensions ($\mathcal{D}$), for the reduced Planck scale ($Λ_{\mathcal{D}}$) of about a TeV. The corresponding values for $Λ_{\mathcal{D}} = 9~\mathrm{TeV}$ turned out to be about $10.33~\mathrm{TeV}$. A significant reduction in the aforementioned limits is observed while the loss gets higher, e.g. for $ζ= 0.35$, $M_{\mathrm{B}}$ reduces to $7.65 (6.82)~\mathrm{TeV}$ at $Λ_{\mathcal{D}} = 1 (9)~\mathrm{TeV}$. These limits change to $12.03 ~(10.88)~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $7.80~ (7.03)~\mathrm{TeV}$ respectively for $ζ= 0~(0.35)$ for $Λ_{\mathcal{D}} = 1 (9)~\mathrm{TeV}$ at 95\% C.L. in case $\mathcal{D}$ is raised to seven.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes microscopic black hole production at the LHC within the ADD model at √s = 14 TeV and 349.4 fb⁻¹ luminosity, providing constraints on black hole mass M_B while accounting for formation loss via parameter ζ. For ζ=0, black holes with M_B ≤ 11.83 TeV are disfavored for D=3 extra dimensions at Λ_D ≈ 1 TeV, reducing to ~10.33 TeV at Λ_D = 9 TeV. Higher loss (ζ=0.35) lowers limits to 7.65 (6.82) TeV at Λ_D = 1 (9) TeV. For D=7, limits increase to 12.03 (10.88) TeV at ζ=0 and 7.80 (7.03) TeV at ζ=0.35 for Λ_D = 1 (9) TeV at 95% C.L.
AI.motivation: To explore the production of microscopic black holes at the LHC in the ADD model and provide constraints on black hole mass while accounting for energy loss during black hole formation, which has not been fully considered in previous analyses.
AI.method: The analysis uses Monte Carlo simulations for the ADD model at √s = 14 TeV with integrated luminosity 349.4 fb⁻¹, incorporating a loss parameter ζ during black hole formation to study its effect on mass constraints.
AI.result: For 3 extra dimensions, ζ=0 disfavors M_B ≤ 11.83 TeV (Λ_D=1 TeV) and ~10.33 TeV (Λ_D=9 TeV); ζ=0.35 reduces these to 7.65 TeV and 6.82 TeV respectively. For 7 extra dimensions, limits are 12.03 (10.88) TeV at ζ=0 and 7.80 (7.03) TeV at ζ=0.35 for Λ_D=1 (9) TeV at 95% C.L.
AI.conclusion: The black hole mass limits are significantly reduced when accounting for formation losses (higher ζ), with the effect being more pronounced for larger numbers of extra dimensions and lower reduced Planck scales.

title: Shadow Completion in Celestial OPEs
summary: We argue that celestial OPEs must be supplemented by shadow-basis operators. Although the shadow transform does not introduce new bulk degrees of freedom, it provides a distinct primary state in the boundary celestial theory. From OPE consistency, we show that the ordinary celestial OPE does not close on Mellin-basis exchanges alone. Rather, the same exchanged bulk particle must also appear through its shadow-basis representative. This leads to a shadow-completed OPE, with the shadow OPE coefficient fixed by the ordinary collinear coefficient through the universal shadow factor. We discuss the corresponding boundary Hilbert-space interpretation, extend this argument to gluons and gravitons, and verify the shadow exchange directly in tree-level regular celestial amplitudes, including a scalar $2\rightarrow n$ analysis and an explicit five-point example.

AI.tldr: Celestial OPEs must include shadow-basis operators for consistency, as ordinary Mellin-basis exchanges alone do not close the OPE. Shadow coefficients are fixed by ordinary ones via a universal factor, and the shadow exchange is verified in tree-level celestial amplitudes.
AI.motivation: The authors identify an inconsistency in celestial OPEs: ordinary Mellin-basis exchanges alone do not form a closed OPE algebra. They motivate the necessity of shadow-basis operators to resolve this incompleteness.
AI.method: The authors analyze OPE consistency in celestial conformal field theory, derive the shadow completion from the shadow transform, fix the shadow coefficient via the universal shadow factor, and verify the formalism using regular tree-level celestial amplitudes including scalar 2→n and a five-point example.
AI.result: The ordinary celestial OPE does not close on Mellin-basis exchanges alone; each exchanged bulk particle must also appear via its shadow-basis representative. The shadow OPE coefficient is determined by the ordinary coefficient times a universal shadow factor. Shadow exchange is explicitly verified in tree-level celestial amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: Celestial OPEs require shadow-basis operators for closure, introducing distinct primary states in the boundary theory without adding new bulk degrees of freedom. The formalism extends to gluons and gravitons, and is confirmed by amplitude computations.

title: Extraction of charmonium branching fractions from $J/ψ\toγη_c$ radiative decays
summary: We assess the tension between theoretical predictions and the values quoted by the Particle Data Group (PDG) for the partial decay width and branching fraction associated with the radiative charmonium decay $J/ψ\toγη_c$. A profile scan over the most recent PDG data depending on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\toγη_c)$ suggests that the correlation between measured branching fractions is compatible with lattice QCD determinations of the partial decay widths $Γ(J/ψ\toγη_c)$ and $Γ(η_c\toγγ)$. We propose a theoretically grounded photon line shape for the radiative decay spectrum and a prescription for the extraction of (product) branching fractions involving the magnetic dipole (M1) transition $J/ψ\toγη_c$. This approach obviates the need to modify the photon energy spectrum line shape using empirical damping functions, as done in the most recent experimental extractions of $\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\toγη_c)$ from the photon line shape, thereby eliminating an inherent ambiguity in the determination of the derived observables.

AI.tldr: The paper assesses tension between theoretical predictions and PDG data for the J/ψ→γη_c decay, proposes a theoretically grounded photon line shape for M1 radiative decays, and eliminates ambiguity from empirical damping functions in extracting branching fractions.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies between lattice QCD predictions and experimental PDG values for the partial decay width and branching fraction of J/ψ→γη_c, and to eliminate ambiguities from empirical damping functions used in experimental extractions.
AI.method: Profile scan over PDG data correlating branching fractions, comparison with lattice QCD determinations of partial decay widths, and proposal of a theoretically motivated photon line shape for M1 radiative transitions without empirical damping modifications.
AI.result: The correlation between measured branching fractions is compatible with lattice QCD determinations. The proposed theoretical line shape obviates the need for empirical damping functions.
AI.conclusion: A theoretically grounded approach to photon line shape eliminates inherent ambiguities in determining branching fractions for the M1 transition J/ψ→γη_c.

title: Cosmological history after higher dimensional inflation
summary: It was proposed that extra dimensions can acquire large size by higher dimensional inflation connecting two large hierarchies in particle physics and cosmology, namely the weakness of the actual gravitational force to the largeness of the observable universe, in terms of one fundamental scale. This proposal is consistent with the observed approximate scale invariant power spectrum of primordial density perturbations only for one or two extra dimensions of around the micron size. Assuming a stabilisation mechanism of the extra dimensions at the end of inflation, here we propose a cosmological history that describes the Universe evolution after the end of inflation up to the reheating temperature, that guarantees the absence of bulk gravitons at earlier times, avoiding their overproduction in the early universe. The proposed cosmological history connects the period of higher dimensional inflation to the beginning of the standard cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a cosmological history connecting higher-dimensional inflation to standard cosmology, showing that extra dimensions can acquire large size via inflation with one or two micron-sized extra dimensions, and introduces a post-inflation evolution that prevents bulk graviton overproduction while ensuring consistency with observed primordial power spectra.
AI.motivation: To connect two large hierarchies in physics (weak gravity vs. large observable universe) using a single fundamental scale via extra-dimensional inflation, and to address the problem of bulk graviton overproduction in the early universe.
AI.method: The authors propose a cosmological history after the end of higher-dimensional inflation up to the reheating temperature, assuming a stabilization mechanism for extra dimensions, ensuring no bulk gravitons exist at earlier times to avoid overproduction.
AI.result: The proposal is consistent with the observed approximate scale-invariant power spectrum of primordial density perturbations only for one or two extra dimensions of around micron size.
AI.conclusion: A viable cosmological history can connect higher-dimensional inflation to standard cosmology, avoiding bulk graviton overproduction, provided extra dimensions are stabilized after inflation.

title: New Avenues of Heavy Neutral Lepton at Muon Collider
summary: With initial state radiation, the multi-TeV muon collider can be regarded as an electroweak boson collider. The dominant production mode of the certain process becomes the vector boson fusion channel, because the corresponding cross section typically increases logarithmically at high energies. This also holds true for new physics beyond the standard model. Within the $U(1)$ gauged extension of seesaw models, the heavy neutral lepton has additional interactions with the new gauge boson $Z'$ and heavy Higgs $H$. In this paper, we investigate the production of heavy neutral lepton $N$ via the new vector boson fusion processes $Z'Z'\to H\to NN$ with and $Z'Z'\to NN$ without heavy Higgs at the multi-TeV muon collider. Different from the canonical vector boson fusion processes $WW/ZZ\to H\to NN$, the new process $Z'Z'\to H\to NN$ is not suppressed by the small mixing angle $α$ between the Higgs bosons. Therefore, these new avenues provide alternative pathways to probe the intrinsic feature of the heavy neutral lepton. We then perform a detailed analysis of the lepton number violation signals via the new vector boson fusion with heavy Higgs $μ^+μ^-\to μ^+μ^- H \to μ^+μ^- NN$ and without heavy Higgs $μ^+μ^-\to μ^+μ^- NN$, followed by $N\to μ^\pm jj$, where the two jets from $W$ boson decay are treated as one fat-jet $J$.

title: $Ξ_{cc}^{++}-Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ Transitions as a Two-Charm-Selective Portal to Ultra-Low-$Q$ Charged Currents
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 1 table + appendix. Comments welcome
summary: The recent LHCb observation of $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ opens the ultra-low-$Q$ transition $Ξ_{cc}^{++}\toΞ_{cc}^{+}$ as an experimentally motivated null test of charged-current new physics. Our two- and three-body analyses show sensitivity to effective baryon-level couplings of $\mathcal{O}(10^{-6}-10^{-7})$ for MeV-scale recoil momenta. We then identify a two-charm-selective charged-current portal whose leading operator has a nonzero matrix element in doubly charmed baryons but vanishes at leading order in pions, nucleons, nuclei, and singly charmed mesons. In this class of models, $Ξ_{cc}^{++}\toΞ_{cc}^{+}$ transitions can provide the leading direct probe of the portal interaction.

title: NLO QCD and EW corrections to semileptonic vector-boson scattering at the LHC
summary: Vector-boson scattering with semileptonic final states has recently been measured at the LHC, and future experiments are expected to further increase the precision of its measurement, calling for adequate theoretical predictions. In this work, we present a calculation of the NLO QCD and electroweak corrections to the process $\text{p}\text{p} \to \ell^+ ν_\ell + 4\text{j}$ in two different fiducial regions relevant for vector-boson scattering. In a fully off-shell calculation, we provide results for the leading electroweak contribution of $\mathcal{O}\left(α^6\right)$ and the corresponding corrections of $\mathcal{O}\left(α^7\right)$ and $\mathcal{O}\left(α_\text{s} α^6\right)$ for fiducial cross sections and a selection of differential distributions.
