title: Two Flavon Froggatt-Nielsen Models with Genetic Algorithms
summary: We present the first systematic and comprehensive scan of two-flavon Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) models, employing artificial intelligence techniques to explore the high-dimensional, mixed discrete-continuous parameter space. Extending the standard single-flavon FN framework to a two-flavon setup in which separate flavon fields couple independently to the up- and down-type sectors, we demonstrate that the relative phase between their vacuum expectation values (vevs) provides a natural and generic source of CP violation absent in single-flavon models. To explore this enlarged model space, we cast the search for phenomenologically viable models as a multi-objective optimisation problem, formulating each experimental constraint as a separate objective, and employ the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III to simultaneously fit all 18 FN charges, 45 Wilson coefficients, and flavon parameters to both the quark and lepton sectors. Our approach requires no separate training phase and identifies phenomenologically viable models orders of magnitude faster than prior reinforcement learning methods. Imposing experimental constraints on CKM and PMNS mixing angles and CP phases, charged fermion masses, and neutrino squared-mass differences, we discover over $100\,000$ unique viable models with a remarkably low duplication rate, indicating that the space of valid two-flavon FN realisations has not been exhausted. Both Normal and Inverted neutrino mass squared orderings are realised, with the relative hierarchy between the flavon vevs producing qualitatively distinct predictions for the effective neutrinoless double beta decay mass $m_{ee}$. We further demonstrate the existence of minimal FN realisations with maximal flavon exponent as small as three, and of models reproducing charged fermion masses to within $6\%$ without any dedicated continuous parameter optimisation.

AI.tldr: This paper uses AI (NSGA-III) to systematically explore two-flavon Froggatt-Nielsen models, discovering over 100,000 viable models that naturally incorporate CP violation via the relative phase between flavon vevs, fitting both quark and lepton sectors simultaneously.
AI.motivation: Extend the single-flavon FN framework to a two-flavon setup to incorporate a natural source of CP violation via the relative phase between flavon vevs, and systematically explore the high-dimensional mixed discrete-continuous parameter space that is intractable with traditional methods.
AI.method: Cast the search as a multi-objective optimization problem using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) to simultaneously fit 18 FN charges, 45 Wilson coefficients, and flavon parameters to both quark and lepton sector constraints.
AI.result: Discovered over 100,000 unique viable models with low duplication rate; both Normal and Inverted neutrino mass orderings realized; minimal FN realizations with flavon exponent as low as 3; models reproduce charged fermion masses to within 6% without continuous parameter optimization; orders of magnitude faster than prior RL methods.
AI.conclusion: The space of two-flavon FN models is rich and not yet exhausted; the relative phase between flavon vevs provides a generic CP violation source; predictions for neutrinoless double beta decay mass m_ee depend on the flavon vev hierarchy.

title: Toward Precision Fragmentation of $Ω_{3Q}$ Baryons: The OMG3Q1.1 Framework
comment: 52 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, 294 references. Includes F-MHOU and F-NPWF uncertainty replicas, threshold-aware HF-NRevo DGLAP evolution, and LHAPDF release at https://github.com/FGCeliberto/Collinear_FFs
summary: Recent experimental advances in the baryon sector, including the observation of doubly charmed states, have renewed interest in the production mechanisms of increasingly heavy hadronic systems, calling for precision and uncertainty-controlled descriptions. We present the OMG3Q1.1 framework for the fragmentation of same-flavor all-heavy $Ω_{3Q}$ baryons in high-energy hadronic collisions. The construction combines diquark-inspired inputs for constituent-heavy-quark and gluon channels with threshold-aware DGLAP evolution within the HF-NRevo scheme. A replica-based strategy consistently quantifies perturbative missing-higher-order effects (F-MHOUs) and nonperturbative wave-function uncertainties (F-NPWFs), yielding the first uncertainty-resolved fragmentation-function set for the $Ω_{3Q}$ sector. The resulting LHAPDF6 grids are employed to investigate semi-inclusive $Ω_{3Q}$ plus jet production at the HL-LHC and future FCC within the (sym)JETHAD environment. The OMG3Q1.1 framework establishes a precision-oriented baseline for rare triply heavy baryons and provides a foundation for future studies of the heavy-flavor baryon landscape.

title: Non-standard decays of vector-like top partners in a $2$-Higgs doublet model at the HL-LHC
summary: Extensions of the Standard Model featuring both an enlarged scalar sector and vector-like fermions arise naturally in a wide class of well-motivated theoretical frameworks. In such scenarios, vector-like Quarks (VLQs) can exhibit non-standard decay modes involving additional Higgs states, giving rise to distinctive collider signatures that remain largely unexplored by existing experimental searches. We investigate the prospects of probing this possibility at the high-luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) through the decay of vector-like top partner ($T$) to charged Higgs ($H^{\pm}$) followed by the decay, $H^\pm\toτν$, producing a final state containing two tau leptons, two $b$-jets, and missing transverse energy. A model-independent collider analysis is performed using global kinematic observables constructed from visible objects and the missing transverse momentum vector to suppress the dominant backgrounds. Polarization-sensitive observables built from the hadronic $τ$ decay products are also examined as complementary probes of the spin-$0$ origin of the $τ$ leptons. The expected discovery sensitivity is evaluated using the Asimov significance for an integrated luminosity of $3$ ab$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=14$ TeV. Our results demonstrate that the $2τ\:+\:2b\:+$ missing $E_T$ channel provides a promising and largely orthogonal avenue to search for non-standard VLQ decays in extended Higgs sectors, with discovery-level sensitivity achievable for VLQ masses up to approximately $1.9$ TeV.

Using kinematic and polarization-sensitive observables, the authors show that VLQ masses up to ~1.9 TeV can be probed with 3 ab⁻¹ of data at 14 TeV.

AI.method: A model-independent collider analysis is performed using global kinematic observables (from visible objects and missing transverse momentum) to suppress dominant backgrounds. Polarization-sensitive observables from hadronic τ decays are used as complementary probes of the spin-0 origin of τ leptons. Expected discovery sensitivity is evaluated using Asimov significance for 3 ab⁻¹ at √s = 14 TeV.
AI.result: The 2τ + 2b + missing ET channel provides a promising and largely orthogonal avenue for searching for non-standard VLQ decays. Discovery-level sensitivity is achievable for VLQ masses up to approximately 1.9 TeV.
AI.conclusion: The proposed channel offers a viable and complementary search strategy for non-standard VLQ decays in extended Higgs sectors at the HL-LHC.

title: Renormalization of axial anomaly in SU(N)$\times$U(1)
summary: Defining $γ_5$ within dimensional regularization remains a fundamental challenge. Larin's prescription addresses this by introducing additional renormalization constants to restore standard and chiral Ward identities. While these constants are known up to four loops in pure quantum chromodynamics, current precision Standard Model phenomenology requires extending these corrections to mixed gauge sectors. In this article, we propose a novel technique utilizing form factors and the universality of infrared divergences to compute these constants. Applying this framework, we present the new three-loop results for the renormalization constants, as well as the pure-singlet contributions to the quark axial-vector form factor, for a mixed $SU(N) \times U(1)$ gauge group.

AI.tldr: The paper extends Larin's prescription for γ5 in dimensional regularization to mixed SU(N)×U(1) gauge groups, using form factors and infrared divergence universality to compute three-loop renormalization constants and pure-singlet quark axial-vector form factor contributions.
AI.motivation: Precision Standard Model phenomenology requires extending the known four-loop Larin prescription renormalization constants from pure QCD to mixed gauge sectors, which remains an unresolved challenge.
AI.method: A novel technique leveraging form factors and the universality of infrared divergences is proposed to compute the required renormalization constants in mixed gauge theories.
AI.result: New three-loop results for the renormalization constants and pure-singlet contributions to the quark axial-vector form factor are obtained for a mixed SU(N)×U(1) gauge group.
AI.conclusion: The proposed technique successfully extends Larin's prescription to mixed gauge sectors, providing necessary higher-order corrections for precision phenomenology.

title: The Simplest Dirac Scoto-Seesaw Realization
summary: We present a simple Dirac scoto-seesaw framework based on the anomaly-free $U(1)_{B-L}$ charge assignment $(-4,-4,5)$ for $ν_R$. This chiral charge assignment naturally accounts for the observed neutrino mass-squared differences, with $Δm^2_{\rm atm}$ generated at tree level and $Δm^2_{\rm sol}$ arising radiatively. After the spontaneous breaking of gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$, a residual $Z_6$ symmetry stabilizes the dark matter candidate. We investigate two minimal realizations of the framework, finding that both normal and inverted orderings are viable in one case, whereas only normal ordering survives in the other, with distinctive features for neutrino observables. Moreover, the chiral nature of the $U(1)_{B-L}$ charges suppresses the dilepton branching fraction of $Z'$, resulting in weaker ATLAS mass bounds than in the conventional vector $B-L$ scenario, thereby easing constraints on the dark sector. We explore the dark matter phenomenology of the singlet scalar and fermionic dark matter candidates. While singlet scalar DM is often severely constrained, the presence of the $Z'$ portal together with annihilation and co-annihilation channels substantially broadens the allowed parameter space. Thus, the framework offers a predictive scenario for neutrino and dark matter phenomenology that can be probed in future experiments.

AI.tldr: A Dirac scoto-seesaw framework with anomaly-free $U(1)_{B-L}$ charges $(-4,-4,5)$ for $ν_R$ explains neutrino mass-squared differences (tree-level atm, radiative sol), stabilizes dark matter via a residual $Z_6$ symmetry, and suppresses $Z'$ dilepton bounds, allowing broader dark matter parameter spaces for singlet scalar and fermionic candidates.
AI.motivation: To construct a predictive Dirac scoto-seesaw model that simultaneously explains neutrino mass hierarchy, dark matter stability, and relaxes collider constraints on the $Z'$ boson via chiral $U(1)_{B-L}$ charge assignments.
AI.method: The paper assigns chiral $U(1)_{B-L}$ charges $(-4,-4,5)$ to three right-handed neutrinos to ensure anomaly cancellation, generates $Δm^2_{\rm atm}$ at tree level and $Δm^2_{\rm sol}$ radiatively, and relies on a residual $Z_6$ symmetry from $U(1)_{B-L}$ breaking to stabilize dark matter. Two minimal realizations are analyzed for neutrino mass ordering and dark matter phenomenology (singlet scalar and fermionic DM).
AI.result: Both normal and inverted orderings are viable in one realization; only normal ordering survives in the other. The chiral $U(1)_{B-L}$ charges suppress the $Z'$ dilepton branching fraction, relaxing ATLAS mass bounds relative to the conventional vector $B-L$ model. Singlet scalar DM is often constrained, but $Z'$ portal with (co-)annihilation channels broadens the allowed parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a predictive, testable scenario linking neutrino masses, dark matter, and $Z'$ phenomenology, with distinctive signatures for future experiments.

title: Addressing uncertainties of model predictions for extensive air showers initiated by high energy cosmic rays
summary: A new Monte Carlo generator of hadronic collisions, QGSb, is applied for studying model uncertainties regarding calculations of the development of extensive air showers (EAS) initiated by interactions of high energy cosmic rays in the atmosphere. More specifically, we investigate possibilities to modify the model predictions for two EAS characteristics mostly used in experimental studies of cosmic ray composition: air shower maximum depth and the muon number at ground level. For all the considered modifications of the model, we discuss in some detail the underlying physics mechanisms and investigate the impact of the changes, regarding a comparison of the model results to relevant accelerator data.

AI.tldr: The paper uses a new Monte Carlo generator (QGSb) to study model uncertainties in simulating extensive air showers (EAS) from high-energy cosmic rays, focusing on modifications that affect the shower maximum depth and muon number at ground level, and comparing results with accelerator data.
AI.motivation: To investigate model uncertainties in EAS development calculations by modifying the QGSb generator, particularly for two key observables used to infer cosmic ray composition: shower maximum depth and muon number.
AI.method: Using the QGSb Monte Carlo generator for hadronic collisions, modifications are applied to the model and predictions for EAS characteristics (depth of shower maximum and muon number) are computed, with underlying physics mechanisms discussed and results compared to accelerator data.
AI.result: Identified possibilities to modify model predictions for air shower maximum depth and muon number at ground level, with detailed discussion of the physics behind each modification and their impact relative to accelerator data.
AI.conclusion: The QGSb generator is a useful tool for studying model uncertainties in EAS development, and the modifications explored affect the two main observables used for cosmic ray composition studies, with validation against accelerator data.

title: Three-particle di-light-cone distribution amplitudes of the $B$-meson in heavy-quark effective theory
summary: We present a systematic study of the three-particle di-light-cone distribution amplitudes (DLCDAs) of the $B$-meson. They are defined through $B$-meson--to--vacuum matrix elements of trilocal HQET operators, in which the light antiquark and the gluon field-strength tensor are located on two back-to-back light rays. In this sense, the DLCDAs generalise the conventional $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes to configurations where soft fields couple to collinear degrees of freedom in two distinct directions. As such, they parametrise the non-perturbative dynamics associated with non-factorisable soft-gluon contributions in rare and non-leptonic exclusive $B$-meson decays. We derive the complete Lorentz decomposition of the matrix elements of generic trilocal operators, identify eight independent DLCDAs, and organise them in a basis of definite twist. Using local operator identities and equations-of-motion constraints, we obtain tree-level relations for their normalisation integrals and first moments in terms of a minimal set of hadronic parameters. These relations allow us to construct simple momentum-space models for all independent DLCDAs. For the leading-twist distribution, we further incorporate the perturbative radiative tail at order $α_s$ and discuss its impact on the resulting parametrisation.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a systematic study of three-particle di-light-cone distribution amplitudes (DLCDAs) of the B-meson, defining them via trilocal HQET operators on two light rays. Eight independent DLCDAs are identified and organized by twist, with tree-level relations derived from operator identities and equations of motion. Simple momentum-space models are constructed, and the leading-twist distribution is extended to include perturbative radiative corrections at O(α_s).
AI.motivation: To parametrize non-perturbative soft-gluon dynamics in non-factorisable contributions to rare and non-leptonic exclusive B-meson decays, which require a systematic description beyond conventional two-particle light-cone distribution amplitudes.
AI.method: Derivation of complete Lorentz decomposition for trilocal HQET operators, identification of eight independent DLCDAs organized by twist, application of local operator identities and equations-of-motion constraints to obtain tree-level normalization and moment relations, and construction of momentum-space models with O(α_s) radiative corrections for the leading-twist case.
AI.result: Eight independent three-particle DLCDAs are identified, tree-level relations for normalization integrals and first moments are obtained in terms of minimal hadronic parameters, simple momentum-space models are constructed, and the leading-twist distribution is extended to include perturbative radiative tail at O(α_s).
AI.conclusion: The constructed DLCDA framework provides a systematic non-perturbative input for describing soft-gluon contributions in exclusive B-meson decays, with the radiative-improved leading-twist model enabling more precise QCD factorization analyses.

title: Dyonic lattices, $θ$-angles and axions in the Standard Model
summary: We investigate the implications of the Witten effect in the Standard Model with a general global gauge group structure and determine the values of the three $θ$-parameters that lead to distinct families of allowed spectra of dyons. We construct and classify the corresponding dyonic charge lattices consistent with the Standard Model gauge structure. This approach enables us to re-derive the known global-group--dependent periodicities of the $θ$ angles and to determine all CP-invariant points in $θ$-space. The electromagnetic subgroup $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ is shown to arise \emph{prior} to electroweak symmetry breaking by factoring out the effect of the anomalous $B+L$ transformations, which reduces the physical $θ$-parameter space from a three-torus to a two-torus. Our phenomenological conclusions include an observation that a discovery of a $U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ monopole carrying non-zero electric charge would determine the last remaining unknown parameter of the Standard Model. Lastly we study how $θ$-space shapes axion physics with emphasis on the axion-photon coupling and show that a single axion is insufficient to render the Standard Model vacuum fully CP invariant.

AI.tldr: This paper examines the Witten effect in the Standard Model, classifying dyonic charge lattices and showing that the electromagnetic U(1) emerges before electroweak symmetry breaking, reducing the physical θ-parameter space from a three-torus to a two-torus, and concluding that a single axion cannot fully restore CP invariance in the SM vacuum.
AI.motivation: To understand the implications of the Witten effect in the Standard Model with a general global gauge group structure, determine the values of the three θ-parameters that lead to distinct families of allowed dyon spectra, and explore how θ-space shapes axion physics.
AI.method: The authors classify dyonic charge lattices consistent with the Standard Model gauge structure, re-derive global-group-dependent periodicities of θ angles, and show that factoring out anomalous B+L transformations reduces the physical θ-parameter space from a three-torus to a two-torus.
AI.result: The electromagnetic U(1) arises prior to electroweak symmetry breaking; the physical θ-parameter space reduces to a two-torus; a discovery of a U(1)em monopole with non-zero electric charge would determine the last unknown SM parameter; a single axion cannot make the SM vacuum fully CP invariant.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the Standard Model's θ-parameter space is more constrained than previously thought, with phenomenological implications for monopole searches and axion physics, specifically that a single axion is insufficient to restore full CP invariance.

title: Theory Calculations for LDMX and LOHENGRIN beyond Coherent Bethe-Heitler Scattering
summary: The Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX), DarkSHINE, and LOHENGRIN are proposed new experiments. They aim to search for missing momentum signals sourced by the direct production of dark photons with masses in the MeV-GeV range in bremsstrahlung processes, in which an electron beam of a few GeV scatters off a fixed target. So far, the signal characteristics, i.e. the behavior of the recoiling electron, have mostly been studied in coherent Bethe-Heitler electron-nucleus scattering with a dark photon that couples only to the Standard Model charged leptons. In this work, we present the calculations of the differential cross sections of all contributing real emission processes up to third order in the electromagnetic fine structure constant and fourth order in the kinetic mixing parameter associated with the dark photon. We consider a dark photon coupling to both the beam electron and the hadronic target and we take into account the scattering off both the target nucleus and its nuclear constituents. Besides real emission processes, we also discuss virtual dark photon contributions and their relevance for the signal prediction. After discussing the different phase space regions and constraints emerging from the experimental setups, we show numerical results of the cross sections and differential distributions, including the signal and dominant background. Within our framework, we find that the LOHENGRIN experiment will require an extension of its HCAL to effectively veto background processes originating from diffractive scattering. Apart from that, the contributions beyond coherent Bethe-Heitler scattering, in the presence of realistic experimental selections, have only a limited effect on the predicted signal and background in the relevant dark photon mass range.

AI.tldr: This paper presents comprehensive calculations of differential cross sections for dark photon production in electron-nucleus scattering, considering processes up to third order in electromagnetic coupling and fourth order in kinetic mixing. It finds that beyond coherent Bethe-Heitler scattering, contributions have limited effect on signal and background predictions, though LOHENGRIN requires HCAL extension to veto diffractive backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To provide accurate signal predictions for proposed dark photon search experiments (LDMX, DarkSHINE, LOHENGRIN) by calculating all contributing real emission processes up to higher orders, including dark photon couplings to both electrons and hadronic targets, and considering scattering off target nuclei and their constituents.
AI.method: Calculated differential cross sections of all real emission processes up to O(α³) and O(ε⁴) in kinetic mixing. Considered dark photon coupling to both beam electron and hadronic target, scattering off nucleus and nuclear constituents, and virtual dark photon contributions. Analyzed phase space regions and experimental constraints.
AI.result: Beyond coherent Bethe-Heitler scattering has limited effect on signal and background predictions for the relevant dark photon mass range under realistic experimental selections. LOHENGRIN requires HCAL extension to effectively veto diffractive scattering background processes.
AI.conclusion: The dominant signal prediction for these experiments remains well-described by coherent Bethe-Heitler scattering. However, the LOHENGRIN experiment needs hardware modifications (extended HCAL) to handle background from diffractive scattering.

title: Revisiting the role of saturation in diffractive vector meson production
summary: We perform a global Bayesian analysis of coherent and incoherent diffractive $\mathrm{J}/ψ$ photoproduction in $γ+p$ and $γ+\mathrm{Pb}$ collisions using a Color Glass Condensate (CGC)-based framework and ultraperipheral collision data from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), corrected for the expected effect of electromagnetic dissociation (EMD). Using Gaussian-process emulators of the underlying CGC calculations, we infer model parameters from a combined set of HERA and LHC measurements. We find that the $γ+\mathrm{Pb}$ data with EMD correction substantially reduce the previously observed tension between proton and nuclear datasets, enabling a consistent simultaneous description of diffractive $\mathrm{J}/ψ$ production in $γ+p$ and $γ+\mathrm{Pb}$ collisions within the CGC framework.

AI.tldr: A global Bayesian analysis of coherent and incoherent diffractive J/ψ photoproduction in γ+p and γ+Pb collisions using a CGC framework, with LHC data corrected for electromagnetic dissociation. Gaussian-process emulators infer model parameters from HERA and LHC data. EMD correction reduces tension between proton and nuclear datasets, enabling consistent simultaneous description within CGC.
AI.motivation: To resolve the previously observed tension between proton and nuclear datasets in describing diffractive J/ψ photoproduction within the Color Glass Condensate framework.
AI.method: Global Bayesian analysis using CGC-based framework with Gaussian-process emulators, incorporating HERA and LHC ultraperipheral collision data corrected for electromagnetic dissociation.
AI.result: EMD-corrected γ+Pb data substantially reduces tension between proton and nuclear datasets, enabling a consistent simultaneous description.
AI.conclusion: The CGC framework can consistently describe diffractive J/ψ production in both γ+p and γ+Pb collisions when EMD corrections are applied to nuclear data.

title: Phase Transitions and Gravitational Wave Production at the End of Thermal Inflation
summary: We investigate the first-order phase transition that terminates thermal inflation and evaluate the associated stochastic gravitational-wave signals. The transition is first characterized through semi-analytic calculations of the bounce action, which are compared with numerical results obtained using CosmoTransitions. We then study its real-time evolution in a three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulation that incorporates Hubble expansion and the corresponding temperature evolution throughout the transition. The lattice dynamics are consistent with the bounce-action estimates: the transition proceeds through localized bubble nucleation and subsequent bubble growth, rather than through a phase-mixing instability. Using the resulting transition parameters, we estimate the gravitational-wave spectra generated by bubble collisions and acoustic motions in the plasma. The predicted stochastic background lies within the projected sensitivity ranges of future gravitational-wave observatories, including BBO and DECIGO.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the first-order phase transition ending thermal inflation, using semi-analytic bounce action calculations and 3D Langevin lattice simulations to characterize bubble nucleation dynamics. The predicted gravitational-wave signals fall within the sensitivity ranges of future observatories like BBO and DECIGO.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature of the phase transition that terminates thermal inflation and evaluate its observable consequences via stochastic gravitational-wave signals.
AI.method: Semi-analytic bounce action calculations validated against CosmoTransitions numerical results, and 3D Langevin lattice simulations incorporating Hubble expansion and temperature evolution.
AI.result: The transition proceeds through localized bubble nucleation and growth (not phase-mixing instability), consistent with bounce-action estimates. Predicted gravitational-wave background lies within the sensitivity range of BBO and DECIGO.
AI.conclusion: The first-order phase transition ending thermal inflation can generate detectable stochastic gravitational waves, offering a potential observational probe of the thermal inflation scenario.

title: New Gauge Forces, Neutron Stars and Schwinger Neutrino Production
summary: We investigate neutrino effects of new long-range forces arising from gauging $B-L$, $L_e-L_{μ/τ}$ or $L_μ-L_τ$ symmetries of the Standard Model. The leptonic potential generated by astronomical bodies, such as the Earth, the Sun or a neutron star, results in the Schwinger pair production of neutrinos charged under the new gauge symmetry. The oppositely charged particles accumulate in the potential well forming a degenerate Fermi gas, while equally charged particles fly away forming a steady flux of neutrinos. We find that, for the $B-L$ and $L_e-L_{μ/τ}$ forces, these effects are too weak to be observable. For the $L_μ-L_τ$ force these effects are significant in neutron stars if the gauge coupling is $g\gtrsim 10^{-18}$. The muonic force changes the element abundances of a neutron star in equilibrium and suppresses its $L_μ-L_τ$ charge. This invalidates the constraint on $g$ from neutron star mergers, at $g\gtrsim 10^{-17}$. Furthermore, for such values of $g$, the neutrino flux produced by the Schwinger effect could potentially be detected from a single young neutron star at a distance of $\simeq 100$ pc, with the typical neutrino energy $E_ν\sim 100$ MeV. A dedicated search for such a signal will reassert the bound $g\lesssim 10^{-18}$.

AI.tldr: The paper studies neutrino effects from new long-range forces (B-L, L_e-L_μ/τ, L_μ-L_τ). For L_μ-L_τ forces with g≳10^{-18}, neutron star effects include Schwinger pair production, degenerate Fermi gas formation, and steady neutrino flux. This invalidates previous merger constraints and could yield detectable ~100 MeV neutrino signals from young neutron stars at ~100 pc, potentially re-establishing bounds at g≲10^{-18}.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether new long-range forces (gauged B-L, L_e-L_μ/τ, L_μ-L_τ symmetries) produce observable neutrino effects via Schwinger pair production in the leptonic potentials of astronomical bodies like Earth, Sun, or neutron stars.
AI.method: The authors analyze Schwinger pair production of neutrinos in the leptonic potential of astronomical bodies. They compute the accumulation of oppositely charged neutrinos forming a degenerate Fermi gas and the flux of equally charged neutrinos escaping. They apply this to three gauge symmetries and evaluate observable consequences for neutron stars.
AI.result: B-L and L_e-L_μ/τ forces produce too weak effects. For L_μ-L_τ forces with g≳10^{-18}, effects are significant in neutron stars: the muonic force alters element abundances, suppresses the L_μ-L_τ charge (invalidating merger constraints at g≳10^{-17}), and produces a steady neutrino flux with E_ν~100 MeV detectable from a single young neutron star at ~100 pc.
AI.conclusion: A dedicated search for the predicted neutrino signal could reassert the bound g≲10^{-18} for the L_μ-L_τ force.

title: The X17 Anomaly: Experimental Evidence and Theoretical Interpretations
summary: This review summarizes the experimental evidence for the hypothetical X17 particle, examines the theoretical frameworks in which it can be accommodated, and discusses its potential implications for the Standard Model and couplings to known particles. Future experimental prospects are also highlighted.

AI.tldr: This review summarizes experimental evidence for the hypothetical X17 particle, examines theoretical frameworks accommodating it, discusses implications for the Standard Model and particle couplings, and highlights future experimental prospects.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the experimental evidence for the hypothetical X17 particle and assess its potential impact on the Standard Model.
AI.method: The paper reviews experimental evidence, examines theoretical frameworks accommodating the X17 particle, and discusses its couplings to known particles.
AI.result: A summary of the current state of experimental evidence for the X17 particle and an analysis of theoretical models that can accommodate it.
AI.conclusion: The X17 particle, if confirmed, could have significant implications for the Standard Model, and future experiments are needed to further investigate its properties.

title: String Axiverse Enhancement of Superradiant Dark Matter Production
summary: We study the effects of string axion emission on dark matter production by light primordial black holes (PBHs), through both evaporation and superradiance. We show, in particular, that the Hawking emission of $\mathcal{O}(100-10^5)$ light axion species predicted in realistic string theory constructions can significantly enhance the efficiency of superradiance, given the associated increase in the PBH spin. The string axiverse thus significantly expands the parametric regions (dark matter mass and PBH mass and spin) for which a sizeable fraction of dark matter may presently be in the form of ``micro-boson stars'': the self-gravitating remnants of superradiant dark matter clouds. Conversely, for too large a number of axion species PBHs evaporate too quickly for superradiant clouds to attain their maximum mass. Finally, assuming that all dark matter is produced by PBHs (through both superradiance and Hawking emission), we show that the axions emitted during PBH evaporation give an immeasurably small contribution to the relativistic degrees of freedom at recombination.

AI.tldr: String axion emission from light primordial black holes (PBHs) enhances superradiance efficiency and expands the parameter space for micro-boson star dark matter, but too many axion species cause premature PBH evaporation; axions from Hawking emission negligibly affect relativistic degrees of freedom at recombination.
AI.motivation: To study how string axion emission affects dark matter production by light primordial black holes through both evaporation and superradiance, particularly exploring the implications of the string axiverse (O(100-10^5) light axion species).
AI.method: Analyzed the effects of multiple light axion species from string theory on PBH evaporation and superradiance, examined parametric regions for micro-boson star formation, and computed contributions to relativistic degrees of freedom at recombination.
AI.result: String axiverse significantly expands parametric regions where dark matter can be micro-boson stars; too many axion species cause PBHs to evaporate too quickly for superradiant clouds to reach maximum mass; axions from PBH evaporation contribute immeasurably to relativistic degrees of freedom at recombination.
AI.conclusion: String axion emissions significantly alter PBH dark matter production dynamics, expanding viable parameter space for micro-boson star dark matter while imposing an upper bound on viable axion species due to premature evaporation, but without observable impact on cosmic microwave background.

title: The $B^+ \to K^+ ν\bar ν$ decay as a QCD axion search: comparing reinterpretation approaches
summary: Two recent independent analyses of Belle II $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$ data yield limits on ${\mathcal B}(B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a)$ -- the two-body mode to a light invisible particle such as the QCD axion -- differing by a factor of roughly four; we trace this to the choice of kinematic variable space. The central figure of merit is the resolution in the reconstructed di-neutrino invariant mass $q^2_{\rm rec}$: fine-grained binning resolves the narrow axion signal, while coarse binning dilutes it into a background-dominated range. A BDT axis trained on $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$ adds little discriminating power for $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a$, as this axis is largely uncorrelated with $q^2$. These expectations are confirmed by a set of numerical tests. The subleading shape systematics omitted from our $q^2_{\rm rec}$-based approach {\em lower}, not raise, the $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a$ limit: by better accommodating the $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$ shape, they leave less room for the axion signal, making our $q^2_{\rm rec}$-based bound conservative, if anything. A dedicated reanalysis confirms that the kinematic-axes choice alone accounts for the factor-of-four sensitivity difference, and that the $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ a$ bound varies sizeably within the $q^2_{\rm rec}\timesη({\rm BDT}_2)$ space, depending on the SM-likeness of $B^+ \! \to \! K^+ν\barν$, thus losing the dual-probe feature of our $q^2_{\rm rec}$-based approach. These results point to a broader consideration: likelihoods dominated by BDT variables are of limited use for reinterpretations when the signal shape differs appreciably from the BDT's training signal. We therefore advocate that experimental collaborations publish likelihood projections in physical variable spaces alongside BDT-based likelihoods, to maximise the reinterpretability of their measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies that a factor-of-four discrepancy in Belle II $B^+ \to K^+ a$ limits arises from the choice of kinematic variable space. Using fine-grained $q^2_{\rm rec}$ binning resolves the narrow axion signal, while BDT-based axes trained on $B^+ \to K^+ \nu \bar{\nu}$ add little discriminating power for the axion signal. The authors advocate for experimental collaborations to publish likelihood projections in physical variable spaces alongside BDT-based likelihoods to improve reinterpretability.
AI.motivation: To resolve a factor-of-four discrepancy between two independent analyses of Belle II $B^+ \to K^+ \nu \bar{\nu}$ data that set limits on the two-body decay $B^+ \to K^+ a$ to a light invisible particle like the QCD axion.
AI.method: Trace the discrepancy to the choice of kinematic variable space; compare fine-grained $q^2_{\rm rec}$ binning vs. coarse binning and BDT axes; perform numerical tests and a dedicated reanalysis in $q^2_{\rm rec} \times \eta(\text{BDT}_2)$ space.
AI.result: The factor-of-four sensitivity difference is solely due to kinematic-axes choice. Fine $q^2_{\rm rec}$ binning resolves the narrow axion signal; coarse binning dilutes it. BDT axes trained on $B^+ \to K^+ \nu \bar{\nu}$ are largely uncorrelated with $q^2$ and add little discriminating power for $B^+ \to K^+ a$. Subleading shape systematics lower the limit, making the $q^2_{\rm rec}$-based bound conservative.
AI.conclusion: Likelihoods dominated by BDT variables have limited reinterpretability when signal shapes differ from the training signal. The authors advocate for experimental collaborations to publish likelihood projections in physical variable spaces alongside BDT-based likelihoods to maximize reinterpretability.

title: Rotating magnetized pion gas of finite transverse size: condensation constraints and transport properties
summary: This work investigates the electric, thermal, and thermoelectric responses of a rotating pion gas of finite transverse radius in the presence of a background magnetic field, with the rotation axis aligned with the magnetic field. We explicitly calculate the parameter limits for $π^+$ condensation and restrict our working regime safely outside these boundaries, ensuring well-behaved transport coefficients. Notably, the system exhibits a condensation asymmetry, with $π^-$ remaining uncondensed at the parameters that induce $π^+$ condensation. Using the Boltzmann Transport Equation under the Relaxation Time Approximation, we calculate the longitudinal electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and the Seebeck coefficient. Our results reveal a competing interplay between the magnetic field and rotation, highlighting the substantial impact of rotation on the medium's transport properties: while the magnetic field suppresses the transport coefficients in a static medium, rotation, acting as an effective chemical potential, introduces an energy shift that favors their increase. Beyond an angular velocity, this rotational enhancement overpowers the magnetic suppression, leading to an increase in the transport coefficients with increasing magnetic field. Finally, we analyze the relative significance of charge and heat transport through the Lorenz number, providing further insight into the transport characteristics of the rotating magnetized pion medium.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the transport properties (electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, Seebeck coefficient) of a rotating pion gas in a magnetic field, finding that rotation can counteract magnetic suppression of transport coefficients and even reverse the trend, with an asymmetry where π⁺ condenses while π⁻ does not.
AI.motivation: To understand the combined effects of rotation and magnetic fields on transport properties of pion matter, relevant for heavy-ion collisions and astrophysical contexts where both strong magnetic fields and vorticity coexist.
AI.method: Boltzmann Transport Equation under Relaxation Time Approximation applied to a rotating pion gas of finite transverse radius with background magnetic field, with careful exclusion of condensation regimes.
AI.result: Rotation enhances transport coefficients by acting as an effective chemical potential, counteracting the magnetic field's suppressive effect; beyond a threshold angular velocity, transport coefficients increase with magnetic field rather than decrease.
AI.conclusion: Rotation fundamentally alters the magneto-transport properties of pion gas, with a competitive interplay between magnetic suppression and rotational enhancement, and an asymmetric condensation behavior between π⁺ and π⁻.
